text: {settlement} has walls and too few people to stand on them; anyone determined would find a stretch that nobody watches.

{settlement} stands where a river comes down to the sea, and its boats work the river more than the coast.
In {settlement} the talk is of the river's moods more than the sea's, though the salt gets into everything.
What {settlement} trades comes and goes by the river; the sea at its back carries less of it.
{settlement} stands at a river's mouth because goods could go up the river and out to sea from the same landing.
{settlement} was put where the river meets the sea, and it has lived off both waters since.
{settlement} began as a landing at the river's mouth, and the landing is still the reason for the place.
{settlement}'s ground gives less than it needs, and what the river brings down and the sea brings in makes up the rest.
{settlement} has few fields between the river and the sea, and it eats from the boats.
Bread in {settlement} comes down the river or in from the sea, because the ground at the mouth was never good for grain.

text: {settlement} keeps stores and is fed by the roads; the roads are the vulnerability, and the granary is what buys time to do something about them.

pool: Logistics & Supply: Granary with road supply
text: An interruption on the roads to {settlement} does not reach the table, and the granary is the reason rather than the roads.

The harbour at {settlement} is full of vessels that cannot leave and empty of the ones that should be coming in.
